title: Read legacy Rails and prove a safe change
outcome: Map a production-style feature, write behavior tests, and explain a change without copying work code.
book: Eloquent Ruby ch. 29; Metaprogramming Ruby part II
cue: Trace one path. Break one promise. Prove one repair.

trace.title: Route entry
trace.detail:
# The idea

Start a legacy feature investigation at its entry point. Find the route, controller action, service, model/query, callbacks, worker, and response presenter.

Draw only the path relevant to the reported behavior. Search for callers before changing a method contract.

Rails 4.2 uses classic autoloading. File paths, constant names, and development reload behavior matter.

Modern Zeitwerk rules cannot be pasted in as if they already run here. Concerns can install callbacks; a method body alone may not show the whole action.

Use model tests for domain rules, request/controller tests for the HTTP boundary, and job/service tests for failure and duplicate handling.

The course examples are new task-tracker examples informed by broad patterns such as services, concerns, SQL boundaries, and workers.

No private work code or real data belongs in these lessons or AI chat.

trace.title: Follow the middle steps
trace.detail:
Capstone: a task can be completed by an allowed member. It creates a receipt intent once.

A worker sends it later. Add a list page with owner names.

Show access denial, validation failure, concurrent completion, provider timeout, and a bounded query count.

Write a two-minute explanation: what enters, what rule holds, which writes commit together, what can repeat, and how you verified it.

Keep a bug diary with symptom → cause → smallest fix → regression test.

trace.title: Check the result
trace.detail:
A broad rescue in a controller can hide a service failure as a 200. A mocked model can make a callback-heavy feature look simpler than it is.

Read the callback registrations and SQL behavior before judging coverage.

recallPrompt: Without notes: Map a production-style feature, write behavior tests, and explain a change without copying work code. Give a concrete failure example.
